reference.title: Dumbbell Incline One Arm Press
reference.listing: Page could not be read (blocked by the network proxy); movement taken from the exercise name and standard coaching practice
reference.note: Reference used only to identify the movement. No GymVisual media is stored here; this rig, model and animation are original.

breathing.pattern: Inhale as you lower the dumbbell, exhale as you press it up.
breathing.cadence: About 2.0 s down, 0.3 s pause, 1.2 s up

prescription.tempo: 2-0-1-0 (2 s down, no pause, 1 s up)
prescription.load: Dumbbell load is user-chosen: pick a weight you can lift for the target reps with 1-3 reps in reserve (RIR 1-3, about RPE 7-9); start a little lighter than one hand of your two-arm incline press.
prescription.progression: Add reps up to the top of the range, then the next dumbbell; finish all reps on the weaker arm first.

cues.text: Back pad at 30 degrees, glutes in the crease, upper back and head on the pad, feet planted wide; one dumbbell up over the right shoulder, palm forward, the free hand resting on the stomach.
Breathe in and lower the dumbbell under control, elbow about 45-60 degrees from the side, forearm vertical; keep the chest square, do not let the trunk roll toward the weight.
Dumbbell beside the upper chest, upper arm just below the bench line; brief pause, no bounce.
Breathe out and press up and slightly in until the arm is straight over the shoulder.
Pause at the top with the shoulder blade still pinned to the pad, then lower again. Switch arms after the set.

mistakes.mistake: Trunk rolling toward the working arm
mistakes.fix: Brace the trunk and plant the opposite foot; both shoulder blades stay on the pad.

mistakes.mistake: Elbow flared straight out at 90 degrees
mistakes.fix: Bring the elbow to about 45-60 degrees from the body.

mistakes.mistake: Bouncing out of the bottom or cutting the range short
mistakes.fix: Lower under control to beside the chest, pause, then press.

mistakes.mistake: Wrist bent back, dumbbell drifting toward the face
mistakes.fix: Keep the forearm vertical under the dumbbell and the wrist straight.
Keep the glutes in the crease and both feet planted.

kinematics.norm: Arm straight but not locked at the top; about 90-110 degrees at the bottom (clinical opinion)

kinematics.measure: Elbow flare (upper arm from the trunk)
kinematics.norm: About 45-60 degrees from the body at the bottom (clinical opinion)
Upper arm just below the line of the back at the bottom (clinical opinion)
Up and slightly in from beside the upper chest to over the shoulder (clinical opinion)
Free hand resting on the stomach (clinical opinion)
Feet flat, knees about 85-90 degrees (clinical opinion)
About 2 s down, a short pause, 1-1.5 s up (clinical opinion)

cautions: Get into position safely: sit with the dumbbell on the right thigh, lie back and kick it up with the knee; at the end of the set bring it back to the thigh rather than dropping it (clinical opinion).
Shoulder pain: shorten the range at the bottom and keep the upper arms out of the fully stretched position until it settles (clinical opinion).
Keep the wrists straight over the forearms; bent-back wrists under a heavy dumbbell strain the wrist.
Stop if sharp pain, numbness or tingling occurs.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
modify: Shoulder discomfort: use a neutral grip (palms facing each other) and tuck the elbows a little more.
Lower back arching too much: put the feet on a low step or the end of the bench.
progressions: Alternating incline press with two dumbbells.

muscleNotes.pec_r: Main pusher, with a shift toward the upper (clavicular) fibres: a 30-degree incline gave the highest upper-pectoralis activity, while the middle and lower fibres fell as the bench was raised (Rodríguez-Ridao 2020, barbell); Lauver 2016 also recommends a 30-degree incline for the pectoralis major.
muscleNotes.ant_deltoid_r: Works harder as the bench rises: at 30 degrees it was about as active as the upper chest, and it became the most active muscle at 45 and 60 degrees (Rodríguez-Ridao 2020).
muscleNotes.triceps_r: Straightens the elbow; triceps activity did not change with bench angle (Rodríguez-Ridao 2020) and is lower with dumbbells than with a barbell (Saeterbakken 2011).
muscleNotes.serratus_r: Holds the shoulder blade against the rib cage while the arm presses.
muscleNotes.biceps_r: Works as a stabiliser: biceps activity rose with the stability demand, highest with dumbbells (Saeterbakken 2011).
muscleNotes.infraspinatus_r: Rotator cuff: centres the head of the upper arm while the dumbbells balance freely (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.rhomboids_midtrap_r: Keep the shoulder blades drawn back and down on the bench.
muscleNotes.core: Bracing keeps the ribs down and the trunk square while only one side is loaded.
muscleNotes.obliques_r: Resist the trunk being pulled toward the loaded side; a one-arm press asks the trunk to resist rotation (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.obliques_l: Resist the trunk being pulled toward the loaded side (clinical opinion).
